title: Seismic vulnerability assessment of existing buildings in Duhok City, Kurdistan Region (KR), Iraq: application of the rapid visual screening method
finding: Rapid visual screening of an estimated 43,000 buildings: nearly 50% highly vulnerable and about 10% at risk of collapse in a major earthquake; results mapped in GIS.

authors: Abduljaleel, Z. A., Taha, B. O., & Yaseen, A. A.
title: Seismic vulnerability assessment of Rizgary Hospital building in Erbil City, the capital city of KR of Iraq
finding: About 120 incremental dynamic analyses: collapse accelerations below 0.2 g against an expected 0.4 g; pounding and irregularities increase vulnerability.

authors: Abdi, A. I., & Yaseen, A. A.
title: Seismic vulnerability assessment of existing RC multi-story buildings in Duhok City, Kurdistan Region of Iraq
venue: Journal of University of Duhok (Pure and Eng. Sciences), 24(1), 60–78
finding: Pushover analysis of six buildings (FEMA 440): weak-column / strong-beam behaviour and damage concentrated in ground-storey columns, which should be strengthened.

authors: Abduljaleel, Z. A., Taha, B. O., & Yaseen, A. A.
title: Seismic vulnerability assessment of reinforced concrete building structures in Erbil City, capital city of Kurdistan Region of Iraq
finding: Over 800 incremental dynamic analyses: collapse capacities of about 0.30–0.35 g (commercial, hotel) and ≤ 0.3 g (residential) against an expected 0.4 g; masonry infill increases vulnerability.

authors: Yaseen, A. A., & Ahmed, M. S.
title: Seismic vulnerability assessment of single-story masonry buildings in Kurdistan Region – Iraq
finding: Single-story URM buildings (about 67% of the building stock) are highly susceptible to slight and moderate damage; extensive to very heavy damage is expected in the eastern KRI.

authors: Abdulsitar, M. S., & Yaseen, A. A.
title: Seismic fragility assessment of vertical hybrid RC frame–masonry buildings using capacity-based damage thresholds derived from pushover analysis
finding: 24 structural cases: collapse probability exceeds 0.5 at 0.25–0.30 g for the more vulnerable configurations, driven by small yield displacements of the masonry.
